items.title: THE COMMODITY PRICE SUPER CYCLE IS IN GEAR.
items.content:
THE COMMODITY PRICE SUPER CYCLE IS IN GEAR.Macro Liquidity by Sunil Reddy (@Macrobysunil)Commodity prices since the Iran war began:

Cocoa +116%
Heating Oil +68%
Gasoline +58%
Rice +41%
Cotton +35%
Wheat +30%
Crude Oil +28%
Sugar +27%
Coffee +13%
Corn +10%
Copper +5%

This is no longer just an Oil story.

The important part is the broadening.

Energy moved first. Now food and agricultural commodities are beginning to participate.

Energy inflation hurts margins.

Food inflation hurts households directly.

And once staples such as Rice and Wheat start rising sharply, the problem quickly moves from financial markets into inflation expectations, politics and social stability.

Energy shock → production costs → transport costs → food prices

The commodity complex is getting much more interesting.—  https://x.com/Macrobysunil/status/2091805118954123562 
— Steve Hanke (@steve_hanke) Aug 25, 2026

items.title: BUY GOLD, WEAR DIAMONDS.
items.content:
BUY GOLD, WEAR DIAMONDS.Global Markets Investor (@GlobalMktObserv)🔥Investors are piling into gold at a historic pace:

Hedge funds, money managers, and other speculative traders added a record +$22.2 billion to their net gold futures exposure over the last 3 weeks, the largest increase in more than a decade, according to Goldman Sachs data.

This was driven by +$13.6 billion in new long positions and +$8.6 billion in short covering, pushing net length to ~$112 billion, higher than roughly 93% of readings over the past 2 years.

Net length measures the value of bullish futures positions minus bearish positions, showing how heavily investors are positioned for higher gold prices.

Furthermore, commodity trading advisor (CTA) positioning in gold, which reflects systematic trend-following funds, flipped from a record short of -10 in early August to a net long of +6.8 in just 3 weeks, the highest reading since March.

Institutional investors are chasing the gold rally.—  https://x.com/GlobalMktObserv/status/2091893879180083419 
— Steve Hanke (@steve_hanke) Aug 25, 2026
